# ShopKit

> A free, open-source Next.js 16 e-commerce template: a 16-product lifestyle-goods
> store with a cart drawer, ⌘K product search, faceted filters, sparkline charts and a
> four-step mock checkout. MIT licensed.

Site: https://shopkit.vivekkumarsingh.in
Source: https://github.com/intellectwithvivek/shopkit
Licence: MIT

Built with VivekUI (@the_viveksingh/vivek-ui), a free React component library with zero runtime dependencies, by Vivek Kumar Singh.

- Docs: https://ui.vivekkumarsingh.in/docs
- npm: https://www.npmjs.com/package/@the_viveksingh/vivek-ui
- GitHub: https://github.com/intellectwithvivek/vivek_UI
- Author: https://vivekkumarsingh.in/

## Using this template

It is free and open source. Three ways to start:

1. Create your own repository from it (no git history attached):
   https://github.com/intellectwithvivek/shopkit/generate
2. Clone it:
   git clone https://github.com/intellectwithvivek/shopkit.git
   cd shopkit && npm install && npm run dev
3. Deploy it straight to Vercel:
   https://vercel.com/new/clone?repository-url=https%3A%2F%2Fgithub.com%2Fintellectwithvivek%2Fshopkit

There is nothing to configure — no environment variables, no database, no API keys. The
one value worth changing is SITE_URL in lib/site.ts, which every canonical URL, the
sitemap, robots.txt and all JSON-LD derive from.

## What this site is

ShopKit is a demonstration storefront and a starting template. It is not a real shop:
no payment provider is connected, no order is ever dispatched, and the catalog in
`data/products.ts` is mock data. The checkout validates input and totals correctly,
then shows an example order number and status timeline.

## Stack

- Next.js 16.3 (App Router, Turbopack, async `params`/`searchParams`)
- React 19, TypeScript 5
- VivekUI 0.5 for every UI element — no Tailwind, no shadcn, no component CLI
- Node.js 20.9+ (22 LTS recommended)
- Zero runtime dependencies beyond React itself

## Pages

- / — storefront: promo countdown, category tiles, trending row with 14-day sales
  sparklines, best-sellers grid, press logos, testimonials, newsletter, FAQ
- /shop — all 16 products with category, price-range, rating and stock filters, sort
  and pagination
- /product/[slug] — 16 statically prerendered product pages: image carousel, 30-day
  price-history sparkline, specs table, reviews, related products
- /checkout — four-step mock checkout (address, shipping, payment, review), noindex
- /built-with — every VivekUI component used, deep-linked to its documentation

## Product categories

Headphones, watches, sneakers and backpacks — four products each, sixteen in total.

## Frequently asked

Q: How long does shipping take?
A: Standard shipping takes 3-5 working days and express takes 1-2. Orders placed before
2pm ship the same day. This is a demo store, so nothing is actually dispatched.

Q: What is the return policy?
A: Returns are free within 30 days of delivery, for any reason, as long as the item is
unworn and in its original packaging. Refunds land 3-5 working days after the parcel
reaches the warehouse.

Q: Is this template really free?
A: Yes. ShopKit is free and open source under the MIT licence. It can be used
commercially, changed in any way, and the footer credit can be removed. Keeping the
credit or starring the repository is appreciated but never required.

Q: Which UI library powers this store?
A: VivekUI (@the_viveksingh/vivek-ui), a free React component library with zero runtime
dependencies by Vivek Kumar Singh. Every element — the cart drawer, the command
palette, the sparklines, the checkout stepper — comes from that one package, installed
with `npm i @the_viveksingh/vivek-ui` and a single CSS import.

Q: Can it take real payments?
A: Not as shipped. Adding Stripe, Razorpay or another provider means replacing the final
checkout step with a real API call.

Q: How do I get a copy of this template?
A: Either press "Use this template" at
https://github.com/intellectwithvivek/shopkit/generate for a fresh repository, or run
`git clone https://github.com/intellectwithvivek/shopkit.git`. Both are free, and the MIT
licence allows commercial use, modification and removal of the credit.

## Install VivekUI

npm i @the_viveksingh/vivek-ui

Then, once, in your app entry point:

import '@the_viveksingh/vivek-ui/styles.css'
